description: Waiwera is the University of Auckland Geothermal Institute's parallel model of high-temperature subsurface flow. It contains numerical formulations for geothermal fluids and phase changes, with PETSc providing solvers and parallel data structures. JSON inputs describe the mesh, rock properties, boundary conditions, sources and time stepping. Outputs use HDF5 and YAML. Geographic coverage and spatial resolution follow the user-supplied geothermal domain; the simulation period and steps are configurable. The Fortran 2003 source is free under LGPL-3.0 and has a public user guide and benchmark instructions. A limitation is that source availability does not supply the site properties or boundary conditions needed for a calibrated reservoir model. Waiwera supports geothermal energy and heat-supply capacity simulations. FEHM (model-fehm) offers related subsurface heat and fluid modelling. The original project received New Zealand research funding and Contact Energy support. No executable or benchmark data was downloaded.
